priority.override_reason: Fresh ranks 1 through 4 remain closed by documented direct-call/frame, numeric ownership, constructor-receiver, and typed-field rejection evidence. The rank-5 tagcloud and independently profiled rank-11 string-validate-input receipts expose one different current matcher cost: generic quantified atoms materialize every candidate MatchState before match_pattern_first can test its continuation. This unit changes that generic first-result handoff only; it is not a retry of the rejected capture-free compiled RegExp program or simple-atom boundary streaming mechanisms.

mechanism.summary: When top-level first-match execution reaches a non-simple quantified RegExp atom, preserve the existing repetition DFS priority but invoke the remaining pattern continuation at each accept state and stop at the first success instead of first collecting every repetition MatchState in a Vec.
mechanism.generality: Admission is solely the existing matcher context: match_pattern_first is executing a quantified atom that did not take its capture-free SimpleAtom route. It has no workload, source path, input length, iteration count, checksum, pattern-text, or expected-result condition. The all-state matcher, reverse matcher, SimpleAtom path, atom parsing, property caches, and every continuation that fails remain semantically unchanged; the new traversal only changes when a candidate is handed to the same continuation.
semantic_risks: preserving ECMAScript leftmost-first priority through alternatives and greedy or lazy quantified groups
preserving capture writes and clearing of captures for zero repetitions before each attempted continuation
preserving the zero-width-loop filter and duplicate-state suppression used by the existing explicit repetition DFS
preserving nested groups, backreferences, lookarounds, Unicode advancement, and all matcher options because match_atom and the continuation remain the existing implementations
preserving RegExp exec, test, match, replace, and lastIndex result protocol through the unchanged RegexpMatch boundary
